spec_match.rationale: The coverage table (which permissions the intervention touches) and abuse-signal list describe browser-internal behavior that has no normative spec — reasonable as reporting, but rows are uncited and unverifiable from the page.

interactive.rationale: Static table + guidance prose. The permissions named are all queryable live (navigator.permissions.query per name) — a live state panel for the visitor's own browser is the obvious missing element.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Sold as 'what developers should do differently'; the actionable half is prose only.

edge_cases.rationale: No live states, no unsupported handling for permission names an engine doesn't recognize (query throws TypeError — itself worth demonstrating).

references.rationale: Feature index links chromestatus; intervention details cite no blog/design-doc sources.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite exists; page anchors nothing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run: renders clean — 0px overflow both classes, zero console errors.

openQuestions.title: Drive the affected-permissions table from live queries
openQuestions.detail: For each listed permission, run navigator.permissions.query({name}) and render the visitor's real state (or the real TypeError for unrecognized names) beside the intervention notes — making the table honest per engine and giving the page its missing interactive core.

guidanceConsulted.query: permission state display per api live
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Show real permission states rather than static claims.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: NOT applied — filed as the question.

summary: Reviewed headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): clean static coverage table for a browser intervention, with no live permission states and no sources. Moderate question filed for a live query-driven panel.
